account:
It is day 1 at six in the morning, and I have just woken at home. Today my recorded business includes office hours at eight, a grain inspection at the mill at ten, lunch at home at noon, council letters at one, tea at the neighbour's dockside cottage at three, another office return at four-thirty, and home at seven. There is also an approved great-hall lighting inspection at six this evening.

The unusual thing is that both builder and neighbour independently urged me to attend that same six o'clock occasion. Builder called it a routine review of newly installed lanterns and their coverage, with no particular problem. Neighbour offered to walk there with me and confirmed it was the same occasion, not another meeting, but deferred questions about attendance and details to builder. Neighbour also mentioned the baker's cheerful lights, supposedly simply to brighten the bakery. I have seen numerous lanterns around the plaza and builder carrying one. None of that proves anything secret, but the repeated invitations and emphasis on lights make me curious whether the inspection is a pretext for some gathering I have not been told about. I do not know its real purpose or who will attend.

Secretary has recorded the inspection and confirmed that neighbour hosts my daily three o'clock tea. Secretary reported no pending correspondence or verified unusual town news. Yesterday evening I tried to ask builder for details, but builder had walked beyond hearing. Freight heard my question about dockside news, but I left for my home appointment before hearing the reply clearly. I should not treat either unheard conversation as evidence. My next priority is to read the appointment book this morning and keep today's appointments, including the hall inspection, while listening for concrete news.
